done_when: While a builder's tests wait in the test line, its agent place is free for another item and it waits for a place again before its round goes on; a free agent place goes first to work near the end (a fix round after a failed test, a review) and a new build last; and no new build starts while more than two times the test places' count of items wait for tests, starting again when no more than the test places' count wait; new and existing client repos get this with the release, and the shipped coordinator guide and worker brief say it

known.title: Restore running status when a builder regains admission

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a builder finishes its test command and resumes the same model process.
This clears `started_at`, but readmission in `_wait` only sets `admitted=True`; the continuing model never calls `started` again. Consequently, `src/forge/mod/hooks/summary.ts:65-66` counts the resumed builder as waiting, while `src/forge/mod/hooks/machine.ts:49,64` hides its live worker details and labels it “starting” for the remainder of the turn. The sibling suspension path at machine.py:243 leaves the timestamp populated, so suspended builders are conversely counted as running. Preserve consistent running/waiting information through both transitions.
Adds work: preserve accurate machine status through test admission; F 3 x H 2 = 6; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Restore running status when a builder regains admission

why: On busy days builders hold agent places while they wait for the test line, so other items cannot start even though those places sit idle (seen: 4 agent places held, 6 items waiting for tests, waits up to 3 hours). The first fix for this merged with no code (issue 1260)
